objective: Compare immediate vs COUNT-then-500ms delay and first vs second genuine UPDATE on the same child, without internal wait/notify/stack/RSS profiling. Condition intervention, not natural-tail capture or product performance acceptance.
authorization: Human approved P8/48children, alternating three pairs, two writes per child, stop after six measured processes.

protocol.update1: UPDATE fork_probe SET v=-1 WHERE id=1
protocol.update2: UPDATE fork_probe SET v=-2 WHERE id=1
protocol.verification: COUNT=1000/SUM=500500 before delay; each UPDATE affects1 and SELECT matches -1 then -2; cleanup; independent prepared children.

measurement: External query timers only; actual idle duration and exact query-call start age since Fork return recorded. No stack capture, timer observer goroutine, internal stage/notify hooks or parent RSS sampler. Explicit 500ms idle uses a cancelable host timer. Same binary and SQL/verification sequence across arms.

decision.tails_only_immediate: Observed timing-condition association; not a proven fix or population probability
decision.tails_in_second: First-write-only explanation insufficient for those observed cases
decision.tails_only_first: Consistent with first-write/elapsed-time differences, not proof of one-time undo initialization
decision.all_outcomes: Report each pair, per-query p50/p95/max and >100/>500 counts, within-child second-minus-first distributions. No extra runs, no product/default change. Owner/queue attribution remains separate.

limitations: The500ms pause changes both DB age and overlap with other starts/cleanup; cannot isolate age from contention.
Second UPDATE follows first UPDATE and verification; data/undo/cache state and elapsed time change together.
No-wait arm now has a second UPDATE: not an exact replay of previous single-write suite.
No internal tracing does not mean zero measurement overhead. No polling/stack observer is introduced.
Single Mac; no native, Ubuntu, adoption or release gate.
